conclusion: Smaller n_ctx shrinks only the attention K/V (24,576 B per cell: 384 MiB at P1's 16384, 96 MiB at 4096) and the compute buffer (327 to 105 MiB); the 327.5 MiB recurrent state is unchanged. Lambda run 20261021T110426Z, 6 arms x (6 cold rounds + 6 restore rounds), 2,880 invocations, 0 errors, 0 class mismatches, $8.45 at list prices. Primary arm c4096 (the smallest size that refuses none of the 231 JevBench public tasks, max 3,936 tokens, nor any request the 4,096-token window admits) against c16384, within CPU part 0xd40 (n=51/48 cold, 42/55 restore): context_init 0.323 -> 0.198 s (-0.126, 95% CI [-0.132, -0.118]); Max Memory Used 5,160 -> 4,883 MB (-277); restored first forward 0.669 -> 0.560 s (-0.109 [-0.114, -0.099]); Restore Duration -0.098 s [-0.124, -0.074]; restore first-request total 3.914 -> 3.714 s (-0.200 [-0.233, -0.168], -5.1%); cold first-request total -0.082 s [-0.150, -0.023] (-0.2%, inside a 36 s request dominated by the S3 download); warm steady state unchanged (-0.006 [-0.018, +0.010]). 0xd0c (n=6/8 cold, 18/5 restore) and 0xd4f (3/4 cold, no restore) move the same way but their headline CIs overlap 0, so by the all-parts rule c4096's status is no-change; host_variability shows every shared round/part cell for context_init and memory negative beyond the control's spread. The effect scales with bytes removed: restored first forward -0.068 / -0.109 / -0.125 / -0.135 / -0.141 s at 8192 / 4096 / 2048 / 1024 / 512 on 0xd40, Max Memory -176 / -277 / -341 / -368 / -387 MB. c1024 and c2048 are improved on every part for the restore first request, but refuse 41 and 36 of 231 JevBench tasks (422, before decode). c512 changes incident-review-4q's answers (max |dp| 0.0035, no choice flip) because 512 splits its 4 questions into two fork groups; c1024 to c8192 answer every request bit-identically to c16384 and to P1's reference. Recommendation: n_ctx=4096 (= the model window): ~0.1 s off the restored first forward, ~0.2 s off the restored request, 277 MB less memory, no capacity loss. Not inferred: no Graviton generation from CPU parts.

p1_requests.note: need = state + longest question (the least n_ctx that answers the request); one_fork_tokens = state + every question (the least n_ctx that answers it in one fork group, P1's path at n_ctx 16384)

capacity.rule: a request needs n_ctx >= state + its longest question (Shim.forward_shared cuts fork groups to fit). The 4,096-token window (head_config max_length) already bounds state + longest question, so n_ctx >= 4096 refuses nothing the window admits; below 4096 a request over n_ctx gets a 422 (e10_entry.ContextTooSmall) before any decode

host.note: Read inside the function from /proc/cpuinfo, /proc/self/auxv, os.sched_getaffinity and /sys/fs/cgroup on each environment's first invocation. 'unknown' = not exposed. No Graviton generation is inferred: CPU part and features are reported as read.

host_variability.method: Within each observed CPU part, compare each arm's median with the control's (c16384, P1's n_ctx) in each round. Arms are sequential waves; round r runs them rotated left by r (cyclic Latin square), which balances position-within-round across arms but is not simultaneous interleaving. A directional outcome needs the delta to exceed the control's within-cell range; a cell with fewer than two control observations is unassessed. Rows without a CPU part are counted, never a stratum. No Graviton generation is inferred from a CPU part.

hypothesis: P1 builds the llama.cpp context with n_ctx=16384. Its attention K/V cache (384 MiB, 24,576 B per cell) and the 327.5 MiB Gated DeltaNet recurrent state are memset by llama_memory_clear before every forward, and at context init; P3 found memset was 9.2% of cold-init CPU samples and 50.4% of the restored first forward. A smaller n_ctx shrinks only the attention K/V (and the compute buffer), so it should cut context_init, the restored first forward, Max Memory Used, and possibly Restore Duration, in proportion to the bytes removed. The recurrent state does not depend on n_ctx (it scales with N_SEQ, unchanged).
